The JNIM fuel blockade and the Azawad offensive are the tests of that hold on Bamako.

grand_strategy.reading: Mali plays the strategy of a junta that has swapped its old friends for new patrons: it expelled France and left ECOWAS, took Russian soldiers and drones, and bet its revenue on gold that the state now runs itself. The bet holds at the centre and fails at the edges, where the Africa Corps has left Kidal, the JNIM blockade chokes the Dakar and Abidjan corridors, and the Azawad front takes the north. Sovereignty is the regime's only proof of legitimacy, so every concession to a neighbour or to Algeria reads at home as a loss, and that is why the rift with Algiers lasted a year. Watch whether Moscow and Ankara keep paying for the north when the gold and the corridor no longer cover the cost.

relations_to.summary: Mali's junta holds 46 Ivorian soldiers arrested in 2022 (three women freed in September 2022). A Bamako court gave them 20-year terms in late December 2022; a pardon followed in early January 2023, and they reached Abidjan that month. Abidjan calls them a backup force for MINUSMA; Bamako calls them mercenaries.

relations_to.summary: The Algerian army said it shot down a Malian drone that entered its airspace near Tin Zaouatine (reported 31 Mar 2025; Algeria says by more than 2 km, Mali says inside Mali). Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger withdrew their ambassadors on 6 Apr 2025, Algeria suspended flights to and from Mali, and Mali filed an ICJ case on 4 Sep 2025.

relations_to.summary: Algeria reopened its airspace to Malian aircraft (10 Jul 2026) and Tebboune announced on 11 Jul 2026 that Algeria's ambassador would return to Mali; Bamako reciprocated. No conditions were stated and the report does not say whether the ICJ case or Algeria's Tuareg mediation resumes.

relations_to.summary: The Alliance of Sahel States: Niger and Mali (with Burkina Faso) left ECOWAS together, effective 29 January 2025, and launched a joint passport and a joint military arrangement. The date of the confederation treaty itself is not verified in this pass; since is the exit date that the joint arrangement followed.

relations_to.summary: Nigeria's ambassador-designate to Mali presented copies of his credentials to Foreign Minister Abdoulaye Diop in Bamako on 6 August 2026; in July the two sides agreed to hold a Joint Commission to revive dormant agreements and a political dialogue on trafficking and shared security, and a Nigerian airline plans a Lagos-Bamako route.

relations_to.summary: Africa Corps, the Defence Ministry's successor to Wagner, keeps about 2,000 men in Mali since Wagner left on 6-7 Jun 2025; it abandoned Kidal under attack (Apr 2026), lost a helicopter to Tuareg fire (Jul 2026) and is accused by HRW of killing nine villagers (Aug 2026). Burkina Faso (about 300 at Loumbila) and Niger are the same deployment.
